svg.title: Digestion & enzymes
svg.desc: The digestive route: Mouth: chewing/amylase. Oesophagus: moves food. Stomach: acid, protease and mixing. Pancreas supplies enzymes; small intestine digests/absorbs; large intestine absorbs water. Egestion: undigested food out. Excretion: metabolic waste out. Enzyme products: Amylase: starch → sugars; made in salivary glands, pancreas and small intestine. Protease: protein → amino acids; stomach, pancreas, small intestine. Lipase: lipid → glycerol + fatty acids; pancreas and small intestine. Specific active sites: Enzymes are reusable protein catalysts. Substrate binds a complementary active site. Warming increases collisions to an optimum; excess heat/extreme pH can denature the active site. Cold slows activity. Bile & absorbed products: Liver makes bile; gall bladder stores it. Alkaline bile neutralises stomach acid. Emulsification makes fat droplets → more surface area for lipase. Bile is not an enzyme. Products build new molecules; glucose can be respired. Food tests: Benedict’s + water bath: reducing sugar → coloured precipitate. Iodine: starch → blue-black. Biuret: protein → purple. Sudan III: lipid → red oil layer. Separate samples; positive/negative controls; goggles and safe heating. Amylase & pH practical: Vary buffer pH; control temperature, concentrations and volumes. Sample onto fresh iodine every 30 s. Endpoint: iodine stays orange-brown. Repeat. Same starch amount: relative rate = 1/time. Shorter intervals improve endpoint resolution.
